claims.text: Trade-off point, interval: running every hour (assumed) keeps the extra load on the sources small, but figures are up to one hour old plus the run time; this fits the two-hour limit only if a run finishes within the hour.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/reporting-design-review.md @ stage-4 lines 80-81; ADR 0031 @ stage-4 line 50

claims.text: The requirements accept figures up to two hours old (assumed).
Each run recomputes the last 3 days (assumed) and replaces those days' rows: a repeated run gives the same result, and a late cancellation or refund still reaches its day.
Each run's reads are short queries over the last 3 days, once an hour, small compared with order placement.
Changes older than 3 days (for example a late refund) do not reach the hourly runs; the review's risk table answers with a full rerun every week (assumed), owned by the backend developer role.
If the reporting database is lost, it is rebuilt from the sources, not restored from a backup; the review's trade-off: no extra backup, at the cost of rebuild time.

The design review lists four trade-off points (interval, batch versus messages, daily totals, rebuild instead of backup) after three rejected options, which cite driver 1 (capacity ordering needs) and driver 3 (shops in their own databases).
OrderMessage (DonHang.Domain/OrderMessage.cs) has exactly four fields: OrderId, CustomerEmail, CustomerName, OccurredAt; no amount and no line items.
Adding amounts and items to order messages is a schema change every reader must accept, and orders placed before the change cannot be read again from the broker.
New fields on an existing message would have to be optional for as long as old-shaped messages remain after a deploy (outbox, queue, dead-letter queue).
claims.source_hint: docs/design/backend-review-checklist.md @ stage-4 line 34; backend.l4.message-schema-evolution Five-line summary line 4

claims.text: An event projection can be rebuilt only from events that were kept, so a read model fed only from messages cannot cover orders whose messages are gone.
Trade-off point, batch versus messages: batches do not change OrderMessage, but are never live figures.
data-ownership.md lists the daily totals per shop as not an owner: a copy in the reporting database; each figure's owner stays Ordering or Payments, in the owners' databases.
A new question daily totals do not answer, such as sales per hour, needs a new summary table filled again from the sources.

ADR 0031 revisit conditions: a requirement for live figures (order messages must then carry amounts); questions daily totals cannot answer in time, needing a store for analytical queries on detailed data.
Following order messages from the start is right when a live sales screen is the driver; a backup is worth keeping when a rebuild would take longer than reports may be down.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0031 revisit conditions lines 58-60; review line 108 (live screen = new requirement)

claims.text: Until a change older than the window is picked up, the report differs from donhang_payments, and donhang_payments is right; a wider window or more frequent full runs would add load on the owners.
claims.source_hint: data-ownership.md line 21 (trust Ordering, Payments); review lines 80-81 (load grows with runs)

claims.text: Figures at most 15 minutes old are still a batch, so the live-figures revisit condition is not met; the load estimate is redone before the interval changes.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0031 lines 58-60; review lines 65-66 (load judged small for hourly runs)

claims.text: For a rebuildable copy, losing it loses no figure for good, so the RPO is zero and the RTO is the rebuild time; if the rebuild takes longer than the team can wait, the rebuild-instead-of-backup point is reconsidered.
Each run replaces its window's rows from the owners, so after a restarted run finishes every day in the window is counted once, whatever a failed attempt wrote.

beyond_scope: Weekly full rerun (assumed) for changes older than 3 days, from the review's risk table; used to answer late refunds outside the window.
